subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the bracketed idiom in the given sentence.

The first sample of ore from the trial boring is very promising, but we should remember that (one swallow does not make a summer.)

options.text: The fact of failure or escape is not affected by the narrowness of the margin
To come out of one trouble and get into a worse
A single fortunate event does not mean that what follows will also be good.

solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"one swallow does not make a summer"** is used to express the idea that one good or successful event does not mean that everything that follows will also be good or successful. (एक फूल के खिलने से बहार नहीं आती).
 
• **"A single fortunate event does not mean that what follows will also be good" **- This is the **correct meaning **of *"one swallow does not make a summer."*
 
• **It means** that one good event does not guarantee that everything else will be good. 

Therefore, the** correct answer** is: *"A single fortunate event does not mean that what follows will also be good"*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's explain all the given words:
 
 
• **"The fact of failure or escape is not affected by the narrowness of the margin" **- This phrase means that whether you fail or succeed is not influenced by how close you are to success or failure. 
 
• **"To come out of one trouble and get into a worse" **- This means to escape from one problem only to encounter an even bigger problem.
 
• **"The whole of everything"** - This phrase means the entirety or totality of something.
